routes.label: Use an isosceles triangle and similarity

officialSolution.label: 2021 AMC 12A
officialSolution.sourceTerms: The linked source retains its printed copyright notice and host terms. This project adds no copy of this PDF.

question: Trapezoid \(ABCD\) has \(AB \parallel CD,\) \(BC = CD = 43,\) and \(AD \perp BD.\) Let \(O\) be the intersection of the diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD,\) and let \(P\) be the midpoint of \(BD.\) Given that \(OP = 11,\) the length \(AD\) can be written in the form \(m\sqrt n,\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are positive integers and \(n\) is not divisible by the square of any prime. What is \(m + n?\)
solution:
The equality \(BC=CD\) makes triangle \(BCD\) isosceles. Its median \(CP\) is therefore perpendicular to \(BD\) and bisects \(\angle BCD\). Since \(AD\perp BD\) as well, \(CP\parallel AD\).

Extend \(CP\) through \(P\) to meet \(AB\) at \(E\). The quadrilateral \(AECD\) has both pairs of opposite sides parallel, so it is a parallelogram. Hence
\[
AE=CD=43.
\]
Because \(CE\) bisects \(\angle BCD\), and \(CD\parallel EB\),
\[
\angle BCE=\angle DCE=\angle CEB.
\]
Thus triangle \(BCE\) is isosceles, giving \(EB=BC=43\). Consequently,
\[
AB=AE+EB=86.
\]

Triangles \(CDO\) and \(ABO\) are similar: their angles at \(O\) are vertical angles, and another pair is equal because \(CD\parallel AB\). Therefore
\[
\frac{DO}{BO}=\frac{CD}{AB}=\frac12,
\qquad DO=\frac13BD.
\]
Since \(DP=\frac12BD\), point \(O\) lies between \(D\) and \(P\), and
\[
11=OP=DP-DO
=\left(\frac12-\frac13\right)BD
=\frac16BD.
\]
Thus \(BD=66\).

Finally, triangle \(ADB\) is right at \(D\), so
\[
AD=\sqrt{AB^2-BD^2}
=\sqrt{86^2-66^2}
=\sqrt{3040}
=4\sqrt{190}.
\]
Since \(190=2\cdot5\cdot19\) is squarefree, \(m=4\) and \(n=190\). The answer is \(\boxed{194}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
